## How I'm reading the two axes

`severity` and `scores.agent_risk` are genuinely orthogonal here, and the split does most of the work in this review:

- **`severity`** — how wrong the code is *now*.
- **`agent_risk`** — how likely the *next* edit is to be wrong, because the code misleads whoever (or whatever) reads it.

Note the agent_risk scale in this scan is compressed: it tops out at **0.44** (`crime_00001`) and bottoms at 0.02. So I band it relatively — **≥0.35 high**, **0.25–0.34 mid**, **≤0.24 low** — rather than reading 0.44 as "44% risky".

My gate:

| Verdict | Rule |
|---|---|
| **Block merge** | The code is wrong outside the author's machine, or two declarations of the same record can silently disagree about money/identity/time. Correctness *now*. |
| **Warn** | Correct today, but raises the odds the next edit is wrong. Ship with a tracked follow-up. |
| **Ignore** | Cosmetic, asset hygiene, or fully absorbed by a blocking fix. |

---

## Block merge — 7 findings

| id | charge | file | sev | agent_risk | why it blocks |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `crime_00011` | Contract Split-Brain (`Invoice`) | `src/api/state.ts:9` ↔ `src/billing.ts:19` | **0.96** | 0.36 | Highest severity in the report. Two `Invoice` interfaces, **6 disagreements** — `subtotalCents`, `taxCents`, `discountCents`, `currency`, `userId`, `createdAt`. Every money field and the owning identifier live on one side only, and evidence is explicit: *"Nothing in the build checks the two declarations against each other."* An agent editing `state.ts`'s `Invoice` gets no type error and silently drops tax. |
| `crime_00010` | Contract Split-Brain (`User`) | `src/api/state.ts:4` ↔ `src/billing.ts:4` | **0.90** | 0.36 | Same class, same file pair, 100% field overlap on the smaller side with `createdAt` present on one only. Fixing `Invoice` without fixing `User` leaves the identical trap next door — cheap to do both in one change. |
| `crime_00018` | Localhost-on-Disk | `src/api/files.ts:9` | 0.60 | 0.30 | `/Users/andrew/dev/crimes/schema.json`. This path exists on exactly one machine. Severity 0.60 understates it — for every other dev, every CI runner, and every deploy this is a hard failure, not a risk. Effort is `quick`. |
| `crime_00017` | Dev-Server URL | `src/api/files.ts:8` | 0.60 | 0.30 | `localhost:3000` in non-test, non-config source. Same file, same class, same `quick` effort. Both of these are "works on my laptop" defects and there is no reason to merge them. |
| `crime_00009` | Half-UTC, Half-Local | `src/date.ts:9,41` | **0.80** | 0.36 | `d.getUTCFullYear()` at L9 and `d.getMonth()` at L41 on the same receiver. This is a live bug, not a smell: the two families differ by the host's UTC offset, so the same input produces different output in CI and in production. |
| `crime_00013` | Timezone Roulette | `src/date.ts:29,33` | 0.60 | 0.35 | `"2026-12-25T07:00:00"` and `"2026-12-20"` — per spec the first parses as **local** and the second as **UTC**. Two literals five lines apart resolving in different time domains, in the same module as `crime_00009`. |
| `crime_00001` | Temporal Recklessness | `src/date.ts:4–40` | **0.80** | **0.44** | Top agent_risk in the entire report. 8 clock reads, and evidence isolates the one that matters: *"1 decide a branch or comparison (line 4)"* — behaviour, not just output. Combined with the two confirmed defects above, `src/date.ts` has no test that can pin it (`test_gap` 0.5). Blocking the whole module together is one `inject a clock` change, not three. |

**The block list is really two changes**: unify the `state.ts`/`billing.ts` contracts, and fix `src/date.ts` end-to-end (which also absorbs `crime_00029` and `crime_00030`). Plus a two-line config lift in `files.ts`.

---

## Warn — 25 findings

Grouped by what's driving the warning.

### High agent_risk, low severity — the "small but misleading" band

These are the ones a severity-only review would wave through, and they're the reason `agent_risk` isn't collapsed into severity.

| id | charge | sev | agent_risk | note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `crime_00002` | Return Shape Roulette (`resolvePaymentResult`) | 0.30 | **0.43** | 3 return shapes, **0% key overlap** at the lowest — `{code,message,ok}` vs `{permanent,url}`, no explicit return type. Second-highest agent_risk in the report on a "low". An agent will confidently destructure the wrong branch. |
| `crime_00003` | Missing Agent Context | 0.60 | **0.42** | No `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, or `SKILL.md` anywhere, while `package.json` declares a `bin`. Nothing tells an agent how to run this repo. `small` effort, and it's the cheapest single reduction in aggregate agent risk available. |
| `crime_00004` | String Sprinkles (`"enterprise"`) | 0.50 | **0.42** | Literal in 4 production files across 4 areas (`api`, `billing`, `jobs`, `ui`). This is duplicated policy waiting to happen — and it sits next to `logic_in_comments` describing an enterprise refund rule. |
| `crime_00005` | Duplicated Navigation Source | 0.60 | 0.38 | `/settings/billing` labelled *Plans* in `registry.ts` and *Billing* in `sidebar.ts`. |
| `crime_00006` | Route Metadata Drift | 0.60 | 0.38 | Same destination named **4 competing ways**: component `PricingPage`, `metadata.title` *Plans*, `<title>` *Subscription*, two nav labels. Fix with `crime_00005` — one root cause. |
| `crime_00007` | Sync I/O in Hot Path | 0.40 | 0.38 | `existsSync`/`statSync`/`readFileSync` in `loadPlanSchema`. Async counterparts exist for all three. |
| `crime_00008` | Option Bag Junk Drawer | 0.30 | 0.38 | `describeCheckout(options)` reads 6 implicit fields incl. `role` and `status` — no way for a caller to know what's required. |
| `crime_00014` | Temporal Recklessness | 0.60 | 0.34 | `billing.ts`, 7 reads — but evidence says *"none decide a branch"*. That's exactly why this warns while `crime_00001` blocks. |

### Authority and side effects hidden behind names

| id | charge | sev | agent_risk | note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `crime_00015` | False Identity (`calculateRefundPreview`) | 0.55 | 0.31 | A function named *"preview"* that calls `saveRefundAudit` and `sendRefundEmail`. **I'd elevate this toward blocking** — an agent invoking it to render a preview sends a real customer email. It stays in warn only because it's correct as written; the name is the defect. |
| `crime_00016` | Logic in the Alibi | 0.50 | 0.31 | *"Only owners can refund enterprise plans unless billing support approves"* — an authorization rule living in prose, with the domain terms absent from nearby code. Unenforceable and invisible to any test. |
| `crime_00032` | Catch and Release | 0.35 | 0.26 | `generateInvoice`'s catch contains only a comment, and the catch declares **no binding**. Scored low because the invoice still generates; warned because it's silent failure in a billing path. |
| `crime_00021` | Commented-Out Corpse | 0.45 | 0.29 | `const legacyRefund = await loadRefund(user.id)` in a comment block, in the same refund area as the two above. Prime material for an agent to "restore". |

### Structure — where severity and agent_risk diverge the other way

| id | charge | sev | agent_risk | note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `crime_00036` | God Function (`generateInvoice`) | **0.90** | **0.11** | 204 lines, 3.4× threshold. Severity is near the top, agent_risk near the bottom — and I think **0.11 undersells it**: `crime_00032` (swallowed error) and `crime_00042` (4 TODOs) both live *inside* this function's line range, which is the concrete form of "an agent editing one section misses another". Warn rather than block: it's legible and unrefactored, not wrong. Per the auto-fix policy, propose — don't split it silently. |
| `crime_00039` | God File (`billing.ts`) | 0.60 | 0.05 | 310 lines vs 300 — 1.0× threshold. Marginal; it clears itself the moment `generateInvoice` is extracted. |

### Tests, deps, and docs

| id | charge | sev | agent_risk | note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `crime_00028` | Test That Proves Nothing | 0.45 | 0.27 | *"renders the enterprise plan"* — **0 expect/assert calls**. It's not a test, it's a smoke run that reports green. |
| `crime_00034` | Test That Proves Nothing | 0.25 | 0.23 | *"creates an invoice"* — 1 weak matcher. Between these two, `billing.ts` has no assertion protecting it at all. |
| `crime_00035` | Phantom Accomplice | 0.25 | 0.22 | `vitest` imported at `src/billing.test.ts`, declared in **no** manifest. **Elevated** — a clean install then `npm test` fails; it only works today via hoisting. `quick` effort, and I'd want it in the same PR. |
| `crime_00033` | Docs-Code Drift | 0.35 | 0.24 | `docs/teams.md:5 → ./setup.md` (not found). |
| `crime_00020` | Concept Alias Drift | 0.55 | 0.30 | *account / organisation / team / workspace* for one "tenant" concept across 5 files — and it lines up exactly with the three orphaned routes below. |

### Remaining warns

| id | charge | sev | agent_risk | note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `crime_00019` | DST-Naive Day Math | 0.60 | 0.30 | `+ 86400000` at `date.ts:52`. Same module as the blockers; fold into that fix. |
| `crime_00023` | Temporal Recklessness | 0.35 | 0.28 | `state.ts:18` — only 1 read, but *"all 1 decide a branch"*. Small, real. |
| `crime_00025` `crime_00026` `crime_00027` | Orphaned Destination ×3 | 0.40 | 0.28 | `/account/subscription`, `/team`, `/workspace/members` — no nav, no doc link, no import. Three unreachable routes in one PR, and they're the same three files feeding `crime_00020`. Wire them up or drop them. |
| `crime_00037` | Unfinished Business | 0.40 | 0.10 | 14 markers in `src/todo.ts` (424/1k LOC — 42× threshold). Nothing here is load-bearing yet. |

---

## Ignore — 10 findings

| id | charge | sev | agent_risk | why |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `crime_00038` | SVG With Embedded Raster | **0.75** | **0.07** | Highest-severity thing I'm ignoring, deliberately. Evidence says the whole SVG is **592 bytes** — the severity ladder is scoring the *pattern*, not this instance. agent_risk 0.07 agrees. Genuine miscalibration; a good `--verdict fp` candidate. |
| `crime_00041` | Oversized Raster | 0.40 | 0.04 | 253.9 KB, the bottom rung of its own ladder (`low ≥ 200 · medium ≥ 500 · high ≥ 1000`). |
| `crime_00040` | Icon-Sized Raster | 0.35 | 0.05 | 32×32 PNG. A preference, not a defect. |
| `crime_00042` | Unfinished Business | 0.20 | 0.02 | 4 markers at 12.9/1k LOC vs threshold 10 — barely over, lowest scores in the report on both axes. |
| `crime_00029` | Date String Sewing | 0.30 | 0.26 | `"…" + .getUTCFullYear()` at `date.ts:41` — the *same line* as `crime_00009`. Absorbed by the blocking fix. |
| `crime_00030` | Host-Locale Drift | 0.30 | 0.26 | `toLocaleDateString()` with no locale, `date.ts:46`. Same module, same fix. |
| `crime_00022` | Unprefixed Boolean | 0.30 | 0.29 | `paid`/`expired`/`stale`. Naming convention. |
| `crime_00031` | Unprefixed Boolean | 0.30 | 0.26 | `disableBilling`/`skipRetry`. Same. |
| `crime_00024` | Plural Mismatch | 0.30 | 0.28 | `users: User`, `invoice: Invoice[]`. Detector self-flags as *"v1 — type aliases and generic types are silently skipped"*, so confidence 0.70 is doing a lot of work. |
| `crime_00012` | Negative Flag Maze | 0.25 | 0.36 | The one ignore I'm least sure about — agent_risk 0.36 puts it level with the contract-drift blockers. `!disableBilling && !skipRetry` is a real double-negative, but it's a single condition on one line in `petty.ts`. Ignoring on blast radius, not on principle. |

---

## Merge decision

**Do not merge as-is.** Two changes clear the entire block list:

1. **One contract source** — have `state.ts` reference `billing.ts`'s `User`/`Invoice` (or share a schema). Clears `crime_00010`, `crime_00011`.
2. **Fix `src/date.ts` as a unit** — inject a clock, pick one time family, make every literal explicit about its zone. Clears `crime_00001`, `crime_00009`, `crime_00013`, and absorbs `crime_00019`, `crime_00029`, `crime_00030`.

Plus a two-line lift of `localhost:3000` and `/Users/andrew/…` into config (`crime_00017`, `crime_00018`), both `quick`.

I'd also want `crime_00035` (undeclared `vitest`) in the same PR — CI can't run green without it — and `crime_00015` (`calculateRefundPreview` sends email) resolved before anyone builds a preview UI on top of it.

**Two caveats on the scan itself:**

- **Coverage gap.** `coverage.warnings` reports 1 file excluded and never read — `.crimes/suppressions.json`. Per the warning's own wording, *"findings in it are absent, not zero."* Worth confirming nothing in this PR is being silenced by a suppression that shipped alongside it.
- **`crime_00038` is the clearest scoring disagreement** — severity 0.75 on a 592-byte asset. If this repo adopts `crimes`, that fingerprint is the one I'd send `--verdict fp` with a note.
